citations.quote: Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.

Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $k$ be a field. Inverse image of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) is exact and $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, where $Rf_*$ is computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements ([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]], [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]). For bounded complexes $A,B$ ([[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]) the derived tensor over $k$ is their signed total tensor ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]), and for bounded $A$ and bounded-below $B$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)$ is computed by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ in a $k$-linear bounded-below injective model $B\to I_B$ ([[def-sheaf-hom]], [[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]). Flasque $k$-sheaves ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) are acyclic for sections on every open set ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The tensor-Hom adjunction and the dg associativity, evaluation and symmetry identities are natural. No bounded-constructibility claim for the internal Hom is made here; that requires the local geometric supplier of the later constructible items.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and
finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models and $B$ in the stated constructible subcategory on the base, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

Let $S$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]), let $k$ be a field
and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $S$
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]]). Then $\mathcal F$ is **locally
constant of finite rank** if every point $x\in S$ has an open neighbourhood
$U\subseteq S$ for which there are an integer $n\ge0$ and an isomorphism of
sheaves on $U$
$$\mathcal F|_U\;\cong\;k_U^{\,n},$$
where $k_U$ is the constant sheaf on $U$ with value $k$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ is
the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to the open subspace $U$
([[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]], [[def-morphism-of-presheaves]],
[[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]]). A sheaf with
this property is also called a **finite-rank local system of $k$-vector spaces**
on $S$. This is a property of the sheaf on the space; no identification of such
sheaves with functors on the fundamental groupoid is part of the definition.

The sheaf $k_U^{\,n}$ is the $n$-fold direct sum of $k_U$ in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces, with $k_U^{\,0}$ the zero sheaf; its sections over
an open $W\subseteq U$ are the locally constant functions $W\to k^n$. The
integer $n$ is quantified locally, so no global rank is asserted and the rank
may differ from point to point; the definition asserts no existence of a global
trivialization. The final sentence records only that a functorial groupoid
presentation of local systems is a different, uncompared object here.

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Let $M\in D^-(\mathcal A)$ and $N\in D^+(\mathcal A)$, with termwise bounded representatives. With supplied bounded-above projective models under [[thm-projective-complexes-model-the-bounded-above-derived-category]], define $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)=Q\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,N)$. Alternatively, with supplied bounded-below injective models under [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]], use $Q\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,I_N)$. The target is $D^+(\mathbf{Ab})$.

Here the cochain form of [[def-hom-complex-of-chain-complexes]] has degree-$r$ term $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(M^i,N^{i+r})$ and differential $du=d_Nu-(-1)^ru d_M$. If $M^i=0$ above $b$ and $N^j=0$ below $a$, nonzero factors require $a-r\leq i\leq b$, a finite interval, and the whole term is zero for $r<a-b$.

This construction is a bifunctor on the declared derived categories. Indeed homotopies in either variable induce Hom-complex homotopies. Replacing a projective model by a homotopy equivalent one therefore changes its Hom complex by a homotopy equivalence. A quasi-isomorphism in the target has acyclic cone, whose Hom from $P_M$ is acyclic by K-projectivity; hence the Hom map is a quasi-isomorphism. This also follows degree by degree from [[prop-morphisms-from-a-homotopically-projective-complex-need-no-roof]], which identifies each Hom-complex cohomology with the corresponding derived Hom. The injective argument uses [[prop-morphisms-into-a-homotopically-injective-complex-need-no-roof]] and reverses the roles of source and target. Thus both variables descend through localization. When both systems exist, the quasi-isomorphisms $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,N)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,I_N)\leftarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,I_N)$ give their natural identification. Either one-sided resolution hypothesis suffices.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. No general local-smallness theorem for unbounded $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be
$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The **tensor-product presheaf**
$$
\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G
$$
is defined by
$$(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)(U) := \mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)$$
for each open set $U \subseteq X$, with restriction induced from the
restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.

The **tensor-product sheaf** is the sheafification of this presheaf:
$$\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G := a(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G).$$

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be
$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The **internal Hom sheaf**
$$
\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)
$$
is the sheaf on $X$ defined by
$$U\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X|_U}(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal G|_U)$$
for each open set $U \subseteq X$.

Restriction to a smaller open set $V \subseteq U$ sends a morphism
$\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ to its restriction
$\mathcal F|_V\to\mathcal G|_V$. Multiplication by a local section
$a\in \mathcal O_X(U)$ acts on a morphism $\varphi$ by either pre- or
post-composition with multiplication by $a$, giving
$\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ the structure of an
$\mathcal O_X$-module.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a locally
compact Hausdorff space, let $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ be the category of sheaves of
abelian groups on $X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]) and let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\longrightarrow\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]],
[[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]). For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on
$X$ define the **compactly supported global sections** of $\mathcal F$ to be the
subgroup
$$\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=\{\,s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F):\operatorname{Supp}(s)\ \text{is a compact subset of }X\,\}\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal F),$$
where the support of a section is the set of points at which its germ is
nonzero ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]], [[def-germ-of-section]],
[[def-compact-space]]). This is a subgroup: the zero section has empty support, negation preserves
support, and the support of a sum is closed in $X$ and contained in the finite
union of the two compact supports, hence compact
([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]).
A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian
sheaves induces a map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ by restriction of
$\Gamma(X,\varphi)$, and this makes $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ an additive functor
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$ ([[def-additive-functor]],
[[def-morphism-of-presheaves]]). Six consistency facts hold; all are immediate
from the definitions, and they record the interface used by the compact-support
calculus.

1. **Well-definedness of $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$.** If $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$
   ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]]), and since the stalk maps of a morphism commute
   with the germ maps, $\varphi(s)_x=\varphi_x(s_x)=0$, so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)$. A support
   $\operatorname{Supp}(t)$ is closed in $X$: if $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(t)$ then $t$ agrees with the zero section on some open
   neighbourhood of $x$, by the description of equality of germs
   ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]]). Hence
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))$ is a closed subset of $X$ contained in the
   compact set $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$; being closed in $X$ it is closed in the
   subspace $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, so it is a compact subset of that compact
   space ([[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]) and therefore
   a compact subset of $X$ ([[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]]), and
   $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ maps $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ into
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal G)$. Composites and identities are computed
   componentwise, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is a functor; it is additive because
   $\Gamma(X,-)$ is.
2. **Sheaves of $k$-vector spaces.** If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of
   $k$-vector spaces, then $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ is a $k$-vector subspace of
   $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$: the support of $c\cdot s$ is
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ for $c\ne0$ and $\varnothing$ for $c=0$, and the
   zero section has empty support. For a morphism $\varphi$ of sheaves of
   $k$-vector spaces the map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ is $k$-linear, since
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is. The higher derived functors below are computed from
   an injective resolution datum on abelian sheaves, so they are abelian
   groups; the degree-zero part is the $k$-vector space
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$.
3. **Left exactness.** For every short exact sequence
   $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\varphi'}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal F''\to0$
   of abelian sheaves the sequence
   $$0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi')}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi)}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$$
   is exact. Injectivity: a monomorphism of sheaves has injective stalk maps
   ([[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]), so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=\operatorname{Supp}(s')$ and a section
   killed by $\varphi'$ has all germs zero, hence is zero. Exactness at the
   middle: the kernel of $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is the image of
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi')$ by left exactness of global sections
   ([[lem-global-sections-left-exact]]); if $s=\varphi'(s')$ has compact
   support, then $s'$ has the same support,
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s')=\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$, because $\varphi'$ is stalk-injective, so $s'$ lies
   in $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate from
   $\varphi\circ\varphi'=0$. Thus $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is an additive left exact
   functor on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]).
4. **The derived functors.** Abelian sheaves on $X$ have enough injectives, and
   the embeddings of [[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]] supply one
   functorial injective resolution datum $\mathcal F\mapsto I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
   on the whole category $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, under the Axiom of Choice
   ([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]). The
   **compactly supported cohomology** of $\mathcal F$ is
   $$H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=H^q\bigl(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr)\qquad(q\ge0),\qquad H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=0\quad(q<0),$$
   the cohomology of the deleted resolution, as in the pattern of
   [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]; for a morphism $\varphi$ we
   write $H^q_c(X,\varphi):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map.
5. **Independence of the datum.** If $J$ is another supplied injective
   resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, then $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from
   $J$ is naturally isomorphic to $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from $I$
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]]);
   the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that comparison follows from AC
   ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum up to this
   canonical natural isomorphism.
6. **Delta functor and the compact case.** Since $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is additive
   and left exact and the datum is defined on all of $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, the
   functors $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$, $q\ge0$, carry connecting maps that make them a
   cohomological delta functor with $R^0\Gamma_c(X,-)\cong\Gamma_c(X,-)$, and
   every short exact sequence of abelian sheaves has a long exact
   compact-support cohomology sequence, natural in the sequence
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor]]). If $X$
   is compact, then for every global section $s$ its support is closed in $X$ by
   fact 1, hence a closed subset of the compact space $X$ and therefore
   compact, so every global section is compactly supported; hence
   $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ for every $q$, where $H^q(X,-)$ is
   the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]
   computed from the same datum.

Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]],
[[def-hausdorff-space]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on
$X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]); this covers in particular every sheaf
of $k$-vector spaces over a field $k$, which is the case used by the
compact-support calculus, and for such a sheaf the groups below are $k$-vector
spaces and the maps $k$-linear. Global sections are written
$\Gamma(X,-)$ ([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]). For a compact subset
$K\subseteq X$ ([[def-compact-space]]) let $i:K\hookrightarrow X$ be the
inclusion and consider the canonical restriction map
$$\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)=(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K),\qquad s\longmapsto s|_K,$$
which sends a global section ([[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]) to
the section of the inverse image sheaf ([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]])
that it induces on $K$. Then $\mathcal F$ is **c-soft**, also **soft for
compact supports**, when this map is surjective for every compact subset
$K\subseteq X$, that is: every section of $\mathcal F$ over a compact subset of
$X$ extends to a global section of $\mathcal F$. For sheaves of abelian groups
$\Gamma_c$ and $H^q_c$ of
[[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]] are the compactly supported
analogues of $\Gamma$ and $H^q$.

Two consistency facts hold; both are immediate from the definitions and from
the extension lemma for sections on a compact set, and they are recorded here
because the compact-support calculus uses the first constantly and the second
for injective sheaves.

1. **Neighbourhood formulation.** By
   [[lem-sections-near-a-compact-set-are-sections-on-that-set]], the target of
   the restriction map is the defining colimit of the
   inverse-image presheaf,
   $(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)=\varinjlim_{U\supseteq K}\mathcal F(U)$, so that
   $\mathcal F$ is c-soft if and only if for every compact $K$ and every open
   neighbourhood $U$ of $K$, every section $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ agrees with a
   global section of $\mathcal F$ on some open neighbourhood of $K$. It
   therefore suffices, for c-softness, to test the extended sections only
   locally near $K$.
2. **Flasque implies c-soft.** If $\mathcal F$ is flasque
   ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) then $\mathcal F$ is c-soft: a class in
   $(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)$ is represented by a section $s$ over an open
   neighbourhood $U$ of $K$, and flasqueness extends $s$ to a global section
   $t\in\mathcal F(X)$ with $t|_U=s$, so $t$ is a preimage of that class.

C-softness is a property of the pair $(X,\mathcal F)$ and not of the sheaf
alone: the compact subsets of the base space are part of the test. Nothing is
assumed about the support of the extended global sections, and c-softness is
not the same condition as flasqueness, only implied by it.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

citations.quote: Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.

Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Its exceptional inverse-image candidate $f^!$ represents the natural Hom transposition $$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,f^!B)$$ for bounded source objects $A$ and bounded-below target objects $B$, and has lower cohomological bound $\inf(B)-d$. When the later geometric theorem proves that $f^!$ preserves the bounded constructible subcategory, this becomes the right adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ there; on that bounded constructible specialization the adjunction unit, counit and resolution comparisons satisfy the triangle, identity and cocycle laws. The proper-support evaluation constructs the counit directly. The proof constructs this adjoint from a finite fibrewise-soft resolution and generator complexes, independently of Verdier biduality; it does not infer an unrestricted $D^+$-source adjunction from the bounded-source generator argument.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a locally
compact Hausdorff space, let $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ be the category of sheaves of
abelian groups on $X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]) and let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\longrightarrow\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]],
[[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]). For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on
$X$ define the **compactly supported global sections** of $\mathcal F$ to be the
subgroup
$$\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=\{\,s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F):\operatorname{Supp}(s)\ \text{is a compact subset of }X\,\}\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal F),$$
where the support of a section is the set of points at which its germ is
nonzero ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]], [[def-germ-of-section]],
[[def-compact-space]]). This is a subgroup: the zero section has empty support, negation preserves
support, and the support of a sum is closed in $X$ and contained in the finite
union of the two compact supports, hence compact
([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]).
A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian
sheaves induces a map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ by restriction of
$\Gamma(X,\varphi)$, and this makes $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ an additive functor
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$ ([[def-additive-functor]],
[[def-morphism-of-presheaves]]). Six consistency facts hold; all are immediate
from the definitions, and they record the interface used by the compact-support
calculus.

1. **Well-definedness of $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$.** If $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$
   ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]]), and since the stalk maps of a morphism commute
   with the germ maps, $\varphi(s)_x=\varphi_x(s_x)=0$, so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)$. A support
   $\operatorname{Supp}(t)$ is closed in $X$: if $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(t)$ then $t$ agrees with the zero section on some open
   neighbourhood of $x$, by the description of equality of germs
   ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]]). Hence
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))$ is a closed subset of $X$ contained in the
   compact set $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$; being closed in $X$ it is closed in the
   subspace $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, so it is a compact subset of that compact
   space ([[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]) and therefore
   a compact subset of $X$ ([[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]]), and
   $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ maps $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ into
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal G)$. Composites and identities are computed
   componentwise, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is a functor; it is additive because
   $\Gamma(X,-)$ is.
2. **Sheaves of $k$-vector spaces.** If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of
   $k$-vector spaces, then $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ is a $k$-vector subspace of
   $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$: the support of $c\cdot s$ is
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ for $c\ne0$ and $\varnothing$ for $c=0$, and the
   zero section has empty support. For a morphism $\varphi$ of sheaves of
   $k$-vector spaces the map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ is $k$-linear, since
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is. The higher derived functors below are computed from
   an injective resolution datum on abelian sheaves, so they are abelian
   groups; the degree-zero part is the $k$-vector space
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$.
3. **Left exactness.** For every short exact sequence
   $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\varphi'}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal F''\to0$
   of abelian sheaves the sequence
   $$0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi')}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi)}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$$
   is exact. Injectivity: a monomorphism of sheaves has injective stalk maps
   ([[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]), so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=\operatorname{Supp}(s')$ and a section
   killed by $\varphi'$ has all germs zero, hence is zero. Exactness at the
   middle: the kernel of $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is the image of
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi')$ by left exactness of global sections
   ([[lem-global-sections-left-exact]]); if $s=\varphi'(s')$ has compact
   support, then $s'$ has the same support,
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s')=\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$, because $\varphi'$ is stalk-injective, so $s'$ lies
   in $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate from
   $\varphi\circ\varphi'=0$. Thus $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is an additive left exact
   functor on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]).
4. **The derived functors.** Abelian sheaves on $X$ have enough injectives, and
   the embeddings of [[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]] supply one
   functorial injective resolution datum $\mathcal F\mapsto I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
   on the whole category $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, under the Axiom of Choice
   ([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]). The
   **compactly supported cohomology** of $\mathcal F$ is
   $$H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=H^q\bigl(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr)\qquad(q\ge0),\qquad H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=0\quad(q<0),$$
   the cohomology of the deleted resolution, as in the pattern of
   [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]; for a morphism $\varphi$ we
   write $H^q_c(X,\varphi):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map.
5. **Independence of the datum.** If $J$ is another supplied injective
   resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, then $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from
   $J$ is naturally isomorphic to $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from $I$
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]]);
   the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that comparison follows from AC
   ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum up to this
   canonical natural isomorphism.
6. **Delta functor and the compact case.** Since $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is additive
   and left exact and the datum is defined on all of $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, the
   functors $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$, $q\ge0$, carry connecting maps that make them a
   cohomological delta functor with $R^0\Gamma_c(X,-)\cong\Gamma_c(X,-)$, and
   every short exact sequence of abelian sheaves has a long exact
   compact-support cohomology sequence, natural in the sequence
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor]]). If $X$
   is compact, then for every global section $s$ its support is closed in $X$ by
   fact 1, hence a closed subset of the compact space $X$ and therefore
   compact, so every global section is compactly supported; hence
   $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ for every $q$, where $H^q(X,-)$ is
   the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]
   computed from the same datum.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. No general local-smallness theorem for unbounded $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.

Let $M\in D^-(\mathcal A)$ and $N\in D^+(\mathcal A)$, with termwise bounded representatives. With supplied bounded-above projective models under [[thm-projective-complexes-model-the-bounded-above-derived-category]], define $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)=Q\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,N)$. Alternatively, with supplied bounded-below injective models under [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]], use $Q\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,I_N)$. The target is $D^+(\mathbf{Ab})$.

Here the cochain form of [[def-hom-complex-of-chain-complexes]] has degree-$r$ term $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(M^i,N^{i+r})$ and differential $du=d_Nu-(-1)^ru d_M$. If $M^i=0$ above $b$ and $N^j=0$ below $a$, nonzero factors require $a-r\leq i\leq b$, a finite interval, and the whole term is zero for $r<a-b$.

This construction is a bifunctor on the declared derived categories. Indeed homotopies in either variable induce Hom-complex homotopies. Replacing a projective model by a homotopy equivalent one therefore changes its Hom complex by a homotopy equivalence. A quasi-isomorphism in the target has acyclic cone, whose Hom from $P_M$ is acyclic by K-projectivity; hence the Hom map is a quasi-isomorphism. This also follows degree by degree from [[prop-morphisms-from-a-homotopically-projective-complex-need-no-roof]], which identifies each Hom-complex cohomology with the corresponding derived Hom. The injective argument uses [[prop-morphisms-into-a-homotopically-injective-complex-need-no-roof]] and reverses the roles of source and target. Thus both variables descend through localization. When both systems exist, the quasi-isomorphisms $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,N)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,I_N)\leftarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,I_N)$ give their natural identification. Either one-sided resolution hypothesis suffices.

Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be locally compact Hausdorff spaces
([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Write
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]])
viewed as modules over the constant ring sheaf $k_X$, and form derived
categories in those sheaves ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]).
For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$, set $f^*=f^{-1}$
([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) and define $f_!F$ on an open
$V\subseteq Y$ to consist of the sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed
support ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]) maps properly to $V$, properness
being that of [[def-proper-continuous-map]] together with its stability lemma
[[lem-proper-continuous-map-stability]]. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
$Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ are computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective
replacements. Tensor means the signed total tensor over $k$
([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) and internal derived Hom is the injective
construction of
[[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]]
([[def-sheaf-hom]]).

Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of
[[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds,
and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put
$K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]],
[[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$,
define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with
open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$.
[[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]]
proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen
resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the
terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible
restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts
a generic six-functor axiom.

The prescriptions are those of Verdier's exposé: $f^*$ is the exact inverse
image, $f_!$ is the sheaf of sections whose closed support is proper over the
base — a presheaf by the local nature of properness, whose sheaf property for every sheaf is proved by the exceptional-adjoint theorem
recorded in `justified_by` — $Rf_*$ is derived from the direct image
[[def-direct-image-sheaf]] on bounded-below injective replacements, and the
terms of the chosen finite resolution are fibrewise $c$-soft, not
necessarily $c$-soft on $X$. Their acyclicity for $f_!$ follows from the
fibre formula in its well-definedness theorem; the restricted fibre sheaves
are compact-support acyclic by
[[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]].
The ordinary-operations lemma also supplies the flasque acyclicity
([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) used to compare resolutions. AC supplies the injective replacements and finite fibrewise-soft
resolution; the proper-support sections, extension by zero and the
exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions. Cohomological
shifts obey $H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A)$ in the convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$. We say that
$\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** if for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every
open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, including the empty cover of
$\varnothing$, the following two conditions hold.

**Locality.** If $s,t\in\mathcal F(U)$ satisfy
$$s|_{U_i}=t|_{U_i}\qquad\text{for all }i\in I,$$
then $s=t$.

**Gluing.** If sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfy
$$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in I,$$
then there exists $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that
$$s|_{U_i}=s_i\qquad\text{for all }i\in I.$$

By locality, such a section $s$ is automatically unique. Thus a sheaf is
exactly a presheaf whose compatible local sections glue uniquely.

citations.proof_quote: 7.1 For one morphism between quasi-projective varieties, choose a locally closed embedding of its source into $\mathbb P^N$ and take the reduced closure of its graph in $\mathbb P^N\times Y$. The graph is locally closed, hence open in that closure; thus the map factors as an open inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ followed by the projective projection $p:\overline X\to Y$. The closure is quasi-projective and $p$ is analytically proper by [F1]. Each algebraic fibre has a deleted-boundary model of dimension at most twice the source dimension by [F3]; [F6] therefore bounds compact-support cohomology of every sheaf on every fibre open by that same integer. Thus the support operations satisfy their required all-fibre-open hypothesis, rather than merely a bound for constructible coefficients. Choose [F1]'s one-map Whitney strata for $p$, respecting the boundary $\overline X\setminus X$ and the finite input supports. Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact; $Rj_*$ is locally computed by the ordinary sections on the open part of [F2]'s controlled link-cone chart, and [F3] and [F4] give the bounded finite, locally constant complex-stratum model and its actual restriction maps. The proper whole-fibre local trivializations of [F2] give, over a small ball in each target stratum, a product with a compact stratified fibre. The same derived product reconstruction used in [F3] identifies the constructible input there with a fibre object constant in the ball direction, so its pushforward is its finite fibre cochain complex constant along that ball. Finitely many target strata give a uniform amplitude bound; ordinary direct-image composition (inverse image is exact, so direct image preserves injectives) and the proper-support factorization of step 4.1 show $Rp_*Rj_*$ and $Rp_*j_!$ compute $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ respectively. All models and comparisons commute with field extension by [F3] and [F4]. For a general separated finite-type map, work over an affine target chart, take a finite affine cover of its source preimage and finite intersections, and apply this construction to their finite disjoint union mapping to the target. Prescribe the needed supports in that one-map construction, obtaining one target stratification for the finitely many terms. The actual finite open-cover derived augmentation of [F5] then assembles ordinary pushforward; its extension-by-zero support resolution of step 4.1 assembles proper-support pushforward. Thus the outputs are bounded algebraically constructible locally on the target and hence globally by a finite affine cover. This proof uses a constructed projective factorization on each quasi-projective piece and proper whole-fibre triviality, rather than inferring whole-fibre control from local source charts. No joint stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram is required. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $S$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]), let $k$ be a field
and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $S$
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]]). Then $\mathcal F$ is **locally
constant of finite rank** if every point $x\in S$ has an open neighbourhood
$U\subseteq S$ for which there are an integer $n\ge0$ and an isomorphism of
sheaves on $U$
$$\mathcal F|_U\;\cong\;k_U^{\,n},$$
where $k_U$ is the constant sheaf on $U$ with value $k$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ is
the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to the open subspace $U$
([[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]], [[def-morphism-of-presheaves]],
[[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]]). A sheaf with
this property is also called a **finite-rank local system of $k$-vector spaces**
on $S$. This is a property of the sheaf on the space; no identification of such
sheaves with functors on the fundamental groupoid is part of the definition.

The sheaf $k_U^{\,n}$ is the $n$-fold direct sum of $k_U$ in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces, with $k_U^{\,0}$ the zero sheaf; its sections over
an open $W\subseteq U$ are the locally constant functions $W\to k^n$. The
integer $n$ is quantified locally, so no global rank is asserted and the rank
may differ from point to point; the definition asserts no existence of a global
trivialization. The final sentence records only that a functorial groupoid
presentation of local systems is a different, uncompared object here.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$. We say that
$\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** if for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every
open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, including the empty cover of

$$s|_{U_i}=t|_{U_i}\qquad\text{for all }i\in I,$$
then $s=t$.

$$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in I,$$
then there exists $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that
$$s|_{U_i}=s_i\qquad\text{for all }i\in I.$$

exactly a presheaf whose compatible local sections glue uniquely.

citations.quote: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced quasi-projective complex
algebraic varieties, and prescribe finitely many closed or locally closed
algebraic subsets in source and target. There exist finite smooth complex
algebraic Whitney (a),(b) stratifications with frontier on $X$ and $Y$
respecting all prescribed subsets, such that each source stratum maps
surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. A further finite algebraic
stratification may be prescribed and refined. The analytic strata are smooth
complex manifolds and the restrictions are smooth submersions. If $f$ is proper
in the analytic topology, in particular if it is a projective algebraic
morphism, the whole restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ over any target stratum is
proper; no restriction of $f$ to a nonclosed individual source stratum is
asserted proper.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be
$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The **internal Hom sheaf**
$$
\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)
$$
is the sheaf on $X$ defined by
$$U\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X|_U}(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal G|_U)$$
for each open set $U \subseteq X$.

Restriction to a smaller open set $V \subseteq U$ sends a morphism
$\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ to its restriction
$\mathcal F|_V\to\mathcal G|_V$. Multiplication by a local section
$a\in \mathcal O_X(U)$ acts on a morphism $\varphi$ by either pre- or
post-composition with multiplication by $a$, giving
$\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ the structure of an
$\mathcal O_X$-module.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.
